title: Tensor pool surge causes cross-tenant cache-index drift and cascading OOMs — evictor rewrite + journaling patch
creator: Riley Park
description:
High-level: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private experienced intermittent GPU OOMs beginning 2026-02-18. Root cause analysis identified a tensor-pool growth pattern that created fragmentation and a subtle index-drift in the KV cache's handle table. The stale handle entries caused evictor thrash and delayed compactions, ultimately pushing some pods past GPU memory and triggering OOMs. Impacted tenants: AcmeApp (hosted), FinSaaS (dedicated), MedGroup (private).

This ticket tracks the engineering work to land an in-runtime fix consisting of: 1) an evictor rewrite to use a bounded async work-queue, 2) a journaling layer to serialize KV-index updates to prevent transient deserialize gaps during heavy churn, and 3) an adaptive backpressure token bucket to slow allocation during compaction pressure. The patch aims to close the window where index drift + fragmentation leads to unrecoverable OOMs while preserving steady-state latency.

Why different from previous fixes: earlier hotfixes addressed single symptoms (aggressive eviction, immediate compaction) which reduced OOM frequency but did not eliminate index inconsistency. This approach adds a small durable journaling step and enforces ordering on index updates so we avoid race-induced tombstones and invalid handles under high churn.
updates: 2026-02-18: First customer alert (AcmeApp) reported sudden token spikes and several inference pods restarted with GPU OOM. Oncall triaged and increased eviction aggressiveness as temporary mitigation.

2026-02-19: Incident escalated after FinSaaS and MedGroup reported similar behavior in separate regions. Repro harness built to simulate multi-tenant tensor churn. Initial heap/core dump analysis pointed to handle index inconsistencies.
2026-02-22: PoC journaling + bounded-queue evictor implemented in internal branch. Local stress tests reduced OOM reproduction rate from 60% to 5% under same load profile.
2026-02-25: Canary rollout (5% of hosted, 10% of dedicated pool) began with a feature-flagged binary. Observed 30% reduction in eviction latency variance, OOM count dropped to zero in canary.
2026-03-04: Private deployment customer (MedGroup) accepted on-prem patch and performed isolated validation in their staging cluster.

2026-03-10: Patch opened for security and performance review. Noted a 2-5% median tail latency increase under microbenchmarks due to journaling write overhead; tradeoff reviewed and accepted by PM/Infra.
2026-03-12: Merge request opened and is currently in review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9876. This ticket marking full-engineering review and release notes drafting.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision 3-node GPU pool with multi-tenant workloads (simulated tenants A/B/C).
Start sustained small-batch inference traffic with many short sessions to exercise eviction (seq_len 256, bursty session churn).
Introduce an allocation spike (sustained high concurrency) for 10 minutes to grow tensor pool and cause fragmentation.
Observe GPU memory graphs and eviction/compaction traces in Grafana; reproduce index-out-of-bounds warnings and stale-handle errors in runtime logs.
mitigations_applied: Emergency: increased eviction aggressiveness and forced compaction schedule for affected clusters (temporary).
Applied feature-flagged canary patch with journaling + bounded evictor to 5% hosted / 10% dedicated while validating.
Offered CPU-fallthrough for most-critical tenants as a temporary soft-fail to avoid total outage.
resolution_plan: Complete code review and perf tuning of journaling buffer sizes (PR #9876).
Run 48h mixed-workload stress across hosted/dedicated clusters with chaos faults enabled.
Coordinate canary ramp to 25%/50%/100% across environment over 7 days with rollback gates (OOM rate, eviction latency, compaction lag).
Publish release notes and customer-facing communication with mitigation steps and expected behavior change.
postmortem_actions: Add automated regression test in CI that simulates handle-table churn and verifies no index drift under high allocation churn.
Add dashboard alert (OOM-rate > 0.1/hour per cluster) and runway metric (eviction-thrash-rate) to trigger auto-rollback and paged alerts earlier.
Document operator runbook for 'tensor surge' including immediate soft-fail steps (reduce concurrency, enable CPU-fallthrough, escalate to runtime oncall).
Schedule a follow-up for allocator redesign spike to reduce fragmentation risk (Q2 roadmap).
risk_considerations: Journaling introduces extra writes on the critical path for index updates which increased median token-latency by ~3% in microbenchmarks. Risk accepted because it eliminates unrecoverable OOM vectors for multi-tenant workloads. There is also risk of increased SSD pressure if journaling persisted to disk in some private installs; current design keeps journaling in fast ephemeral NVMe on dedicated hosts and in-memory durable ring for hosted. We'll revisit if Private customers require HSM-backed durability.
test_plan: Unit tests for index update ordering and tombstone reclamation.
Integration tests with the kvcache simulator to assert no stale-handle regressions for 100k ops/s for 1h.
End-to-end stress with tenant mix from production trace replay for 48h.
Performance benchmark (latency/throughput) before/after with 95/99/99.9 p90/p99 comparisons.
customer_notifications: 2026-02-19: Initial incident acknowledgement sent to affected customers with temporary mitigations and next steps.
2026-02-26: Follow-up technical update with PoC results and planned patch timeline.
2026-03-12: Pre-release notice and rollback plan communicated; invited dedicated customers to early upgrade window.
